angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 710,607 km at 42.88 pc = 0.22 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 23.3216 +/- 0.0218 mas (same row, RUWE 1.01): 42.88 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.021 (1.001 to 1.042) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 710,607 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.913 (0.873 to 0.953) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5592 +/- 2.7 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 951427000863064192: teff_gspphot 5592.4697 K (16th-84th percentiles 5589.76-5595.2583), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 951427000863064192: teff_gspphot 5592.4697 K (16th-84th percentiles 5589.76-5595.2583), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/nervia.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.380, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 49674 (pscomppars): spectral type G5 V, from Butler et al. 2003 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2003ApJ...582..455B/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 49674: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 49674 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.32 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 49674 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.02162, from Wright et al. 2007 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2007ApJ...657..533W/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of HD 49674 (pscomppars): age 3.62 Gyr, from Sanz-Forcada et al. 2010 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2010A%26A...511L...8S/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/A+A/684/A28/tablea1 (Evolution of lithium in FGK dwarfs), column Prot: 28 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place. The middle of 2 catalogued periods, 2 of them within 20% of it

spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.021 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.228. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
